content:
kevin: quick idea dump — can we replace per-prefix eviction scans with a stamped ring + small leaky counters to make demotes O(1) and spread work?

maria: curious, high level?

kevin: ring = circular array of buckets for next-N epochs. each prefix maps to one slot via hash(prefix) ^ epoch. when activity happens we bump a tiny counter on the prefix and optionally move its stamp to a later slot (promote). eviction workers just sweep the current slot and demote candidates.

leah: sounds similar to timing wheels. how do counters avoid hot prefixes being demoted too early?

kevin: two levers: 1) 4-bit saturating counter per prefix (0-15) representing recent hotness; 2) on hit we bump counter and optionally shift stamp forward by delta = min(counter, max_shift). so hot prefixes keep hopping forward.

sam: 4-bit? collisions? memory per prefix?

kevin: target ~2 bytes per prefix for stamp+counter: stamp_index: u16 (12 bits used), hot4: u4, flags: u4 => pack to 2 bytes (we actually store in a 32-bit word for alignment). vastly smaller than full lease.

maria: how do we handle correctness (writes) if a demote runs while a writer is mid-pin?

kevin: demote is soft: when we remove residency we set a demote_epoch on the prefix word and start a short grace window (configurable ms). any pin checks both residency and demote_epoch; if demote_epoch present they will attempt a CAS to re-pin or wait for grace expiry.

leah: CAS again on hot path — does that introduce contention?

kevin: CAS only when theres a race (demote_epoch set). common hot paths skip CAS because stamp moved. designed to be optimistic.

sam: migration story? we have an existing lease table with richer metadata.

kevin: 3 migration paths: on-touch convert (preferred), background compactor (low mem spike), or bulk offline transform. on-touch means first load of a prefix reads full lease and initializes compact stamp+counter.

maria: what about multi-tenant fairness and tenant-weighted eviction?

kevin: keep tenant_bucket (2 bits) in a small side table keyed by prefix_hash -> weight_bucket. during demote decision, p_demote = base_p * weight_factor(bucket). side table is tiny (1B/entry) and can be sharded separately.

leah: what about fairness with writes—if tenant A has bursty writes they might keep bumping and starving B. any global fairness?

kevin: we can add a token-bucket per-tenant that slow-downs promotions if a tenant exceeds burst credits in a window. configuration knob.

maria: sketching pseudo: 
```
on_request(prefix):
  stamp = read_stamp(prefix)
  if stamp.slot != current_slot: return
  if read_counter(prefix) < demote_threshold: demote_candidate(prefix)
  else: // hot - reschedule
    new_slot = (current_slot + min(counter, max_shift)) % RING_SZ
    write_stamp(prefix, new_slot)
```

leah: ring size choice? large ring => less jitter, small => more churn. any defaults?

kevin: default ring slots = 32 (covers 32 epochs). epoch length = 1s => 32s window. configurable per deployment.

sam: observability — what metrics to track?

maria: demotes/sec, reinstates/sec, stamp_moves, ring_sweep_time, collisions (hash collisions causing slot overflow), tenant_starve_alert.

ops-bot: deploy-check: add feature flag `ring-evict-v1`, add alert if reinstates/sec > 1% of gets for 5m.

kevin: testing plan: unit tests for counter overflow, racey demote+pin via fuzz harness, large-scale loadbench with synthetic skew, and tenant credit exhaustion test.

leah: any interaction with prefix KV prefetch/pinning APIs?

kevin: APIs unchanged — internal runtime translates pin requests to bump+stamp_move operations. only change is compact storage/backing semantics.

maria: outstanding concerns: 1) how to back pressure stamp moves under heavy write storms, 2) ensuring on-touch migration doesn't amplify latency spikes.

kevin: for (1) we rate limit stamp_moves per node and fall back to a cheap counter-only bump (no atomic stamp write). for (2) use async convert where first-touch serves stale full-lease read but schedules background compact write. callers can opt into blocking convert for strong consistency.

sam: any security/compliance implications? side table with tenant_bucket must not leak tenant mapping across customers.

maria: side table stored encrypted at rest and access controlled by runtime. ops: ensure ACLs.

ops-bot: ticket created: ENG-RT-5678 ring-evict RFC + canary dashboard request.

kevin: next steps: I'll produce an RFC with diagrams and state machine, leah + sam to design tests and bench harness, maria to draft rollout/metric gates. plan to prototype in feature branch next week.

leah: ack.

sam: ack.

maria: thanks all, this looks promising :thumbsup:
